issues.description: Method SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(Meal): the problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies calculateTotalPrice should return a double (use double precision to calculate net cost), but the reference solution declares the method as returning an int (public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal)). This return-type mismatch between the specification and the solution is a genuine contradiction that can confuse students about which signature to implement and may lead to incompatible method signatures between students' code and any reference callers/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the inconsistency by aligning the reference implementation with the problem statement: change the solution method signature to public static double calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal) and perform accumulation with a double (e.g., double sum = 0.0; sum += ingredient.getPrice();). Update any call sites in examples/tests if they assume an int. Alternatively, if integer prices are intentionally required, update the problem statement/UML to state the method returns int and remove references to double precision.
